purpose: Same-condition head-to-head comparison of selective-protection spatial strategies.
tile_grid: same 64x64 tiling and edge handling as SRACR-Med
budget_matching: SRACR defines the actual per-image protected-pixel target after tile rounding; each alternative selects a prefix whose cumulative pixel area is closest to the same target.

policies.sracr_saliency: ResNet-18 Grad-CAM-derived spatial order (same within-image order as reliability-weighted saliency because Q_S is a positive image-level scalar).

same_visibility_proxy: protected tiles replaced with RGB 127 for the residual-information attack endpoint
same_inference_statistics: 2000 bootstrap resamples; 10000 paired sign-flip permutations; Holm correction

aes_execution_control.implementation: single shared AES-256-GCM tile-encryption routine; selector changes only tile IDs
aes_execution_control.note: The residual-leakage attack uses neutral masking at the selected locations rather than rendering ciphertext as image pixels. AES-GCM round-trip correctness is evaluated separately; cipher choice is not varied among policies.

why_no_separate_raw_gradcam_baseline: Reliability Q_S is a positive scalar per image, so it does not change within-image tile ranking at a fixed budget; raw Grad-CAM and SRACR spatial order are therefore identical for this head-to-head test.
why_no_entropy_tile_baseline: Predictive entropy/uncertainty is image-level and does not define a spatial tile ordering at a fixed within-image budget; it is evaluated in controller/risk ablation rather than as a spatial selector.
